chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Shu'ayb from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): He was asked about a man who had a mudarabah (partnership) or a wadi'ah (deposit) or orphans' wealth or merchandise with him, and he had a salaf (advance payment/loan) for some people; he died and left one thousand dirhams or more than that, and what was due to the people from him was more than what he left. He said:
"The wealth is divided among those whom you mentioned, all of them, according to their shares."

Because the first report only included that if the item is present in its own specific form, it is returned to its owner and the creditors do not compete with it for it. And the second [report] contains only that he left one thousand dirhams and upon him were debts and salaf and other things, so he said it is divided among them by shares. And there is no contradiction between the two reports.

key_terms.سَلَفٌ: Salaf (advance payment or loan given in advance)

ai.seo_question: How are specific deposits and general debts distributed when a person dies leaving insufficient funds to cover all obligations?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the distribution of an estate by distinguishing between specific assets held in trust (such as deposits or partnership shares) and general debts. He rules that specific assets are returned directly to their owners without being pooled with the general estate, while the remaining cash is distributed proportionally among all creditors, thereby harmonizing narrations that appear to contradict each other regarding the priority of specific versus general claims.
